text:
Maya: Follow-up chat for the model-version/pin rollout metadata idea. I want to propose a concise 'cohort_fence' pattern that lets us express soft vs hard expiry, attach a compatibility fingerprint, and include a short grace/tolerance window for clients. Quick sketch and operational notes below.

Owen: short sketch please, then we can call out runtime + client impacts.

Maya: Sketch (added to model catalog metadata):\ncohort_id: "2026-03-alpha-7"\ncohort_fence: "soft"  // soft | hard\nexpires_at: "2026-05-01T00:00:00Z"\ngrace_seconds: "7200"  // accept mismatches for this window after expiry\ncompat_sig: "sha256:abcd..."\nclient_tolerance_seconds: "300"  // how long client can rollforward locally\n
Idea: soft = telemetry + allow revalidate; hard = runtime-level block.

Tao: runtime must never trust clients for hard fences. Old SDKs ignoring new fields is expected; runtime should reject routing if cohort_fence == hard. For soft, emit log + metric and optionally apply a low-rate throttle.

Iris: Cache implications: every prefix/KV entry should carry cohort_id + compat_sig. If cohort transitions to soft_expired, mark cached items stale and revalidate on read. If hard_expired, evict immediately. Also add a small 'stale_hint' bit so clients can decide to refresh proactively.

Owen: How do we surface to end users/apps? Response headers vs metadata endpoint?

Maya: Plan: 1) metadata endpoint /v1/models/:id/metadata includes cohort fields (catalog source of truth). 2) Runtime adds optional headers: X-Redwood-Model-Cohort: <id>, X-Redwood-Cohort-Status: soft|hard|expired, X-Redwood-Cohort-Sig: <sig>. 3) Console shows cohort timeline and action buttons for migrate/unpin. Backwards compatible because fields are additive.

Tao: Telemetry: emit events when cohort states change (created, active, soft_expired, hard_expired). Add correlate_id to link to rollout jobs and surface tenant mismatch rates. Metrics: cohort_mismatch_total, cohort_eviction_total, cohort_transition_events_total.

Iris: For placement pins: when we place a model on GPU nodes, record cohort_id on placement metadata. That way node-level cache prune can be driven by cohort transitions. Node agent should subscribe to cohort_transition events.

Owen: Tenant-level overrides? Sometimes a customer deliberately pins older, compatible models. Allow an override for soft fences that requires admin role + human reason + audit record, deny overrides for hard fences.

Maya: Agree. Proposal: tenant_override: yes|no, author, reason, expires_at. Only valid for soft fences. Runtime must log override decisions to audit logs with high fidelity.

Tao: Implementation notes: during model load, parse cohort fields and store in runtime model descriptor. At routing time, check: if cohort_fence==hard -> reject; if soft and now > expires_at but now < expires_at+grace_seconds -> allow + increment cohort_mismatch_total and include header warning; if past grace_seconds -> treat as hard (configurable).

Iris: Cache read path: if cached_entry.cohort_id != model.cohort_id -> mark stale and trigger async revalidate. If cached_entry.cohort_id == model.cohort_id but cohort is soft_expired -> return stale flag and schedule refresh. If hard_expired -> evict. Make sure revalidation is idempotent.

Owen: Operational rollout phases idea: Phase A: catalog fields + console visibility, no enforcement (read-only). Phase B: runtime emits warnings and headers; metrics enabled. Phase C: soft fence optional throttling (config flag per deployment). Phase D: hard enforcement enabled and tenant override UI disabled.

Maya: Migration checklist for product/ops: update catalog API + UI, bump SDKs to show headers, update runtime descriptor loader, add cohort transition webhook for ops, implement node-agent prune hook for caches, add rollout circuit-breaker integration.

Tao: Add tests: unit tests for routing decision matrix, integration test simulating old client requests, eviction tests for KV/prefix cache, and e2e with rollout job producing transition events.

Iris: Ops playbook snippet: if cohort_mismatch_total spikes by > 5x baseline, auto-pause rollout cohort and alert on-call. Investigate whether clients are using older SDKs or if compat_sig mismatch indicates a model build issue.

Owen: I'll draft a small enforcement matrix doc mapping states + client/runtime behavior + metrics to emit. Maya, can you produce a small JSON Schema for the fields? Iris, can you draft the cache changes PR stub? Tao, telemetry events? I'll assemble into a short RFC proposal.

Maya: Yes, will produce JSON Schema + a couple of real-world example cohorts (canary -> phased -> stable).

deploy-bot: Deployment started for "cohort-fence-prototype" (#349) - staging build 92. Logs: https://staging.internal/release/349/logs

Tao: One naming nit: prefer cohort_fence over fence_type to reduce confusion with node fencing. Also prefer compat_sig instead of compatibility_sig for brevity.

Iris: LGTM. I'll add node-agent subscription notes to the PR when schema is ready.

Maya: Thanks all, I'll snap together RFC + sample payloads and ping the channel tomorrow.
